title: Linux platform observation boundary
description: Objective: land the production Linux platform observation/classification surface that task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275 will later certify. Deliverable: a shared platform contract plus Linux adapter and public runner seam under packages/runner/src/platform/**, with focused tests and the consumer task ID recorded. NOT in scope: claiming execution on Linux, spawning processes, producing conformance/fault evidence, changing doctor output, or weakening Windows behavior. Owned paths: packages/runner/src/platform/** and the minimal @moe/runner root export/surface-test wiring. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner test.
definitionOfDone: A frozen, non-empty production boundary vocabulary covers provider launch, Git/workspace and path/symlink observation, locks, signals/cancellation, runtime closure, and crash-recovery observation; tests assert the exact hand-written set and count.
Linux observations classify caller-supplied facts as PROVEN or UNKNOWN with stable reason codes and the PLATFORM_LINUX layer; missing, hostile, stale, or off-host facts never become PROVEN.

The adapter composes existing runner provider, workspace/scope, cancellation, and recovery contracts without copying lifecycle or authority semantics, and contains no child_process/spawn/kill/clock/random environment probing.

@moe/runner exposes a loadable public Linux platform seam, and task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275 is recorded as the real conformance consumer (task-e94b2055e281489ea9e97820919f6856 consumes only the shared contract, not Linux facts).
pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0 with each refusal test asserting its exact reason code and refusing layer.
taskRails: This is an implementation task, not Linux conformance evidence; completion must say host facts remain UNKNOWN unless actually observed by a later real-host task.
Keep the shared contract OS-neutral and Linux classification separate; macOS cannot inherit Linux facts.
No direct process launch, shell command, wall clock, randomness, or environment probing inside the pure runner adapter.

implementationPlan.description: OS-NEUTRAL CONTRACT. Create packages/runner/src/platform/platform-contract.ts and its one-line sibling platform-contract.js (`export * from "./platform-contract.ts";`). It must contain no OS name anywhere except the `PLATFORM_LINUX` layer member, and no classification logic. Contents: `PLATFORM_OBSERVATION_VERSION = "moe-platform-observation/1"`; frozen hand-written `PLATFORM_BOUNDARIES` with exactly these seven members in this order — PROVIDER_LAUNCH, GIT_WORKSPACE, PATH_SYMLINK, LOCK, SIGNAL_CANCELLATION, RUNTIME_CLOSURE, CRASH_RECOVERY — covering the seven areas DoD 1 names; frozen `PLATFORM_LAYERS` = [PLATFORM_CONTRACT, PLATFORM_LINUX] so a refusal can say whether the OS-neutral shape gate or the Linux classifier answered; frozen `PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES` = [PROVEN, UNKNOWN]; frozen `PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES` = [PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN, PLATFORM_FACT_MALFORMED, PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT, PLATFORM_HOST_MISMATCH, PLATFORM_FACT_STALE, PLATFORM_FACT_UNPROVEN, PLATFORM_ARCH_UNSUPPORTED, PLATFORM_CLOSURE_UNPINNABLE, PLATFORM_COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE], each with a `(typeof X)[number]` alias. Types: `PlatformHostIdentity {os, arch, osVersion}` declared here, NOT imported from either provider adapter; `PlatformFailure {ok:false, code, layer, boundary, message}` with factory `platformFailure(code, layer, boundary, message)` returning a frozen object, plus `isPlatformFailure`; `PlatformBoundaryVerdict {boundary, truthClass, failure: PlatformFailure|null}`; `PlatformObservation {observationVersion, host, verdicts, truthClass}`. One OS-neutral gate: `platformBoundaryRejection(boundary, layer)` returning PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN for a name outside the frozen list, and a `platformHostRejection(host, layer)` shape check built on canonical.ts's `isNormalizedText` — shape only, it must not know what 'linux' means. Comment the WHY on the two-layer split and on why the host identity is declared here rather than imported.

No adapter imports either provider's PlatformIdentity; PlatformHostIdentity is declared locally with the why commented.

THREE ADDITIONS BEYOND THE STEP TEXT, each forced by step 1's measurement rather than chosen:

1. `PlatformFactEnvelope<Fact>` + PLATFORM_ENVELOPE_KEYS. Four of the seven composed contracts (WorkspaceInputManifest, MirroredLeaseRecord, ClaudeReconciliation, CrashClassification) carry NO host and NO instant, so the plan's per-boundary gates "embedded host agrees" and "fresh against asOf" have nothing to read on them. The caller states host/observedAt/truthClass alongside the fact and the adapter classifies the envelope. Without this, three of the DoD's twelve classification cases are unexpressible.

2. `snapshotExactRecord(value, keys)`. Reads each key EXACTLY ONCE into a null-prototype snapshot and validates that snapshot, which is what actually defeats the hostile "getter answers differently on a second read" case — a validate-then-read implementation passes that test while recording the attacker's second value. Rejects on own-key-count mismatch, so an extra key and a JSON.parse-injected own `__proto__` are both refusals, not things to ignore. Exported from the module for the adapter's use but NOT destined for the root seam, so it adds no public surface. Deliberately not `exactRecord` from supervisor/effect-shape.ts, per the plan's rejection of that import.

3. `platformHostRejection` takes an optional third `boundary` argument so a malformed host inside a per-boundary envelope can name the boundary it spoiled. Default null preserves the planned two-argument call.

`platformFailure` returns a frozen object; `PlatformFailure.boundary` is `PlatformBoundary | null` because PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN by construction has no valid boundary to name.

LAYER SPLIT IS LOAD-BEARING AND TESTABLE: platformBoundaryRejection/platformHostRejection are shape gates and will be called with PLATFORM_CONTRACT; "is this host linux", "is this arch supported", "is this fact fresh/proven" are Linux judgements and will answer as PLATFORM_LINUX. That is what makes DoD 5's "which layer refused" assertable rather than decorative.

Sibling platform-contract.js written per house convention (`export * from "./platform-contract.ts";`). No test run this step by design; the contract is exercised by the step-3 suite.

Aggregate rule: exactly one UNKNOWN verdict forces aggregate UNKNOWN. Closed-vocabulary sweep: collect every code the suite produced into a Set and assert `set.size > 0` AND `set.size === PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES.length`, so a code nobody can reach cannot be added.

FOUR ASSERTIONS BEYOND THE PLAN, each closing a hole the plan's list left open:

1. "refuses an accessor-backed envelope without ever invoking the accessor" asserts `reads === 0`. The plan's hostile case was a getter that answers differently on a SECOND read, but a read-once-then-validate implementation passes that case while still recording the attacker's value. Asserting zero invocations pins the actual defence. This forced a contract change: snapshotExactRecord now lifts values out of `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and rejects any accessor property, instead of reading `value[key]`.

2. "refuses a fact observed after asOf as PLATFORM_FACT_STALE rather than crediting it". A future observedAt is the obvious way to dodge a staleness gate implemented as a subtraction; without this, `age < 0` silently reads as fresh.

3. "separates a declared absence from an omitted boundary". FACT_ABSENT and COVERAGE_INCOMPLETE would otherwise be the same input (omit one boundary == cover only six). The input's `facts` is an exact 7-key record: an explicit `null` is a declared absence, a MISSING key is a coverage gap. A caller must positively state what it did not observe.

4. Two PLATFORM_CONTRACT-layer cases (unusable host record, non-canonical asOf) that assert `observation.host` is NULL. Forced a second contract change: `PlatformObservation.host` is now `PlatformHostIdentity | null`, because reporting an invented empty-string host would put a fact on the observation that nobody supplied.

CLOSED-VOCABULARY SWEEP is self-contained: `reachableErrorCodes()` drives all nine codes out of the production surface in one function rather than accumulating across tests, so it does not depend on vitest's declaration order. Asserts `size > 0`, `size === PLATFORM_ERROR_CODES.length`, AND sorted set-equality with the vocabulary.

FIXTURES COMPOSE REAL CONTRACTS, no reimplementation: real CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_VERSION, SCOPE_OBSERVATION_VERSION, WORKSPACE_INPUT_MANIFEST_VERSION, CLAUDE_RECONCILIATION_VERSION constants imported from their owning modules, and MirroredLeaseRecord / CrashClassification / ProviderRuntimeObservation typed against their real declarations, so a field drifting is a type error here rather than a silent pass.

API the adapter must now satisfy: `observeLinuxPlatform(input: unknown): PlatformObservation` and `classifyLinuxBoundary(boundary: unknown, envelope: unknown, context): PlatformBoundaryVerdict | PlatformFailure`. Both take unknown at the hostile-input boundary, matching the house convention set by `classifyCrash(inputValue: unknown)` (crash-classification.ts:189) and `parseMirroredLease(value: unknown)`. The union return is what lets an unusable boundary NAME refuse without fabricating a verdict whose `boundary` field must be a valid member.

implementationPlan.description: LINUX ADAPTER — make it green. Create packages/runner/src/platform/linux-observation.ts and its one-line .js sibling. Flat filename on purpose: do NOT create platform/linux/, that directory belongs to task-e87a735386f643fe92c0eeff09bc4275. Exports: `PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER = "PLATFORM_LINUX"`, frozen `LINUX_SUPPORTED_ARCHITECTURES` = [x64, arm64], `ObserveLinuxPlatformInput`, `observeLinuxPlatform(input): PlatformObservation`, and `classifyLinuxBoundary(boundary, fact, context): PlatformBoundaryVerdict`. The input composes existing contracts by TYPE and never re-declares them: providerLaunch as `ProviderRuntimeObservation`, scope as `ScopeObservation`, workspace as `WorkspaceInputManifest`, lock as `MirroredLeaseRecord`, cancellation as `ClaudeReconciliation`, crash as `CrashClassification`, pathSymlink as a contract-declared boundary fact; plus caller-supplied `host: PlatformHostIdentity`, `asOf` and `maxFactAgeMs`. Gate order, and it is load-bearing: host shape -> host.os === 'linux' -> arch supported -> coverage complete -> per-boundary (present -> shape/hostile -> embedded host agrees -> fresh against asOf/maxFactAgeMs -> composed contract's own truth). An off-host input must short-circuit before any per-boundary classification, because a Linux verdict about a win32 fact is meaningless. Aggregate truthClass is AND across all seven: one UNKNOWN makes the whole observation UNKNOWN, and nothing anywhere may raise an UNKNOWN back to PROVEN. Map a provider observation's truthClass onto PLATFORM_TRUTH_CLASSES rather than aliasing it — PROVEN from the provider is a candidate that still has to clear host, arch and freshness. Hard prohibitions from task rail 3, all verifiable by grep on the finished file: no `child_process`, `spawn`, `exec`, `kill`, `Date.now`, `new Date`, `Math.random`, `process.platform`, `process.env`. Freshness compares two caller-supplied canonical timestamps only. Use canonical.ts guards for hostile input; do not import `exactRecord` from supervisor/effect-shape.ts. Keep the file <=250 physical lines by `wc -l`; if it crosses, split the per-boundary classifiers into `platform/linux-boundary.ts` + `.js` — that split is pre-approved, do not trim behaviour to fit.

SPLIT INTO FOUR MODULES, NOT ONE, BECAUSE THE SINGLE FILE MEASURED 385 LINES. The plan pre-approved a `linux-boundary.ts` split and said not to trim behaviour to fit; one split was not enough, so I took two more along the same seam rather than compressing logic. Final `wc -l`, every production file at or under the 250 target:
  linux-boundary.ts   148  gate ORDER only: classifyLinuxBoundary, envelope gating, freshness
  linux-facts.ts      239  per-boundary payload classifiers, payload types, PLATFORM_LINUX_LAYER, linuxRefusal
  linux-observation.ts 163  top-level gates, input types, aggregate

  platform-instant.ts   44  instant arithmetic
Dependency order is acyclic: observation -> boundary -> facts -> contract, and boundary -> instant. Each `.ts` has its one-line `.js` sibling.

GATE ORDER IS EXACTLY THE PLAN'S, and the short-circuits are enforced rather than incidental. Top level: input shape -> host shape -> asOf/maxFactAgeMs shape -> host.os === "linux" -> arch supported -> facts coverage -> per boundary. An off-host or wrong-arch input returns before ANY per-boundary classification runs. Per boundary: absent -> envelope shape -> envelope host usable -> envelope host matches declared -> observedAt/truthClass shape -> freshness -> caller's own truthClass -> composed payload.

LAYER ATTRIBUTION IS REAL, not decorative. Shape failures (input record, host record, asOf) answer as PLATFORM_CONTRACT; host/arch/coverage/freshness/payload failures answer as PLATFORM_LINUX; an unknown boundary NAME answers as PLATFORM_CONTRACT from `platformBoundaryRejection`. Both layers are reachable and the suite pins which one spoke in every refusal.

UNKNOWN IS A FLOOR. Aggregate truth is AND across all seven, and the length check is part of the rule rather than a sanity assertion: `verdicts.every(...)` is vacuously true on a short list, so a truncated verdict set would otherwise read PROVEN. There is no path that raises a verdict after the fact.

MAPPING, NOT ALIASING: a ProviderRuntimeObservation's own `truthClass === "PROVEN"` is checked LAST, after the envelope has already had to clear host identity, host match and freshness. A provider PROVEN never short-circuits anything.

COMPOSES, NEVER COPIES. LOCK is validated by the production `parseMirroredLease`; the other payloads are pinned to their owners' real version constants (CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION_VERSION, SCOPE_OBSERVATION_VERSION, WORKSPACE_INPUT_MANIFEST_VERSION, CLAUDE_RECONCILIATION_VERSION) and to RUNTIME_PINNING_METHODS. No lifecycle or authority semantics are re-derived. `exactRecord` from supervisor/effect-shape.ts is NOT imported, per the plan.

TWO DEFENCES WORTH FLAGGING TO QA:
1. A `CrashClassification` whose kind is "REFUSED" is refused as PLATFORM_FACT_UNPROVEN. A recovery layer that declined to classify is not evidence about a platform, and accepting it would launder a refusal into a proof.
2. `payloadRejection`'s switch has no `default`. The declared return type makes an unhandled boundary a COMPILE error; a default clause would turn a future eighth boundary into a silent pass.

RAIL 3 PROVEN BY GREP, not asserted: `grep "child_process|spawn|exec(|kill|Date\.|new Date|Math.random|process.platform|process.env" platform/*.ts` returns 4 hits, all of them comments stating the prohibition, plus `CANONICAL_INSTANT.exec(value)` which is RegExp.prototype.exec. Freshness is `canonicalEpochMillis(asOf) - canonicalEpochMillis(observedAt)` over two caller-supplied instants, converted by proleptic-Gregorian arithmetic (Hinnant days_from_civil). I deliberately did NOT use `Date.parse`, which is pure and would have been defensible, because a module that already knows how to read a clock is one edit from reading one.

`platform/linux/` and `platform/macos/` were NOT created.

Adding the type names alone failed typecheck with `src/index-surface.test.ts(45,1): error TS6192: All imports in import declaration are unused` -- every other type block in that file is consumed by test code further down. Rather than delete the block, I wrote the consumer: "lets a consumer drive the Linux platform seam using root exports alone". It builds a LinuxBoundaryFacts and an ObserveLinuxPlatformInput from root types only, calls runner.observeLinuxPlatform, narrows the refusal to assert PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT at PLATFORM_LINUX, then classifies a coherent PATH_SYMLINK envelope to PROVEN and an unusable boundary name to PLATFORM_BOUNDARY_UNKNOWN at PLATFORM_CONTRACT.

That test is the answer to the exact defect the canary thread has been arguing about all session: reaching a symbol proves a name is published, DRIVING it proves the published type closure is sufficient to compose against. A cardinality check cannot tell you the difference. It also proves PROVEN is reachable through the root, so the UNKNOWN verdicts elsewhere are a judgement rather than the only answer the seam can give.

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, ONE REAL FINDING FIXED, THEN COMMITTED BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC.

FINDING (fixed): `classifyLinuxBoundary` hardened `boundary` and `envelope` against hostile input but TRUSTED `context`. A caller passing `{host: null, ...}` would dereference null and THROW out of a published root export instead of refusing -- the one outcome a consumer cannot fail closed on, and a direct epic rail 4 violation on the seam this task exists to publish. Two of three parameters defended is worse than none, because it reads as defended.
FIX: signature is now `context: unknown`; `readClassificationContext` validates exact keys plus a usable host, canonical asOf and a safe non-negative maxFactAgeMs, returning a frozen copy so the classifier compares the bytes it checked. Refusal is PLATFORM_FACT_MALFORMED at PLATFORM_CONTRACT naming the boundary. New test sweeps five hostile contexts (non-canonical asOf, Infinity age, negative age, null host, missing key) with `expect(hostile.length).toBe(5)` so the sweep cannot silently generate zero.
DRILL (g) on the fix: replacing the guard with `readClassificationContext(context) ?? (context as ...)` -> "× refuses a hostile classification context instead of throwing out of the seam", 1 failed | 32 passed. Reverted; green.

Also removed a duplicated freshness-age predicate: `isFactAgeMs` now lives once in linux-facts.ts and is used by both entry points.

CHECKLIST ANSWERED:
- Omission vs malformation: absent -> PLATFORM_FACT_ABSENT, malformed -> PLATFORM_FACT_MALFORMED, both UNKNOWN. There is no input where leaving a field out scores better than supplying a bad one.
- Double-read getter: impossible. `snapshotExactRecord` lifts values out of `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and REJECTS accessor properties, so a hostile getter is never invoked even once; the test asserts `reads === 0`.
- UNKNOWN raised to PROVEN: no path. Aggregate is AND, and the length check is part of the rule because `every` on a short list is vacuously true.
- Concurrency/TOCTOU/cleanup: not applicable -- every function is pure, no IO, no shared mutable state, no handles. Vocabularies are frozen; every returned observation, verdict, failure and host is frozen.
- Numeric edges: Infinity/NaN/negative maxFactAgeMs all refuse via Number.isSafeInteger. Post-dated facts refuse as STALE rather than credit.
- Prototype pollution: snapshots are Object.create(null) and key lists are fixed literals; a JSON-injected own `__proto__` trips the own-key-count check.
